ui: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game UI ATLAS for Embers of Before, a gothic pixel-art adventure about fire, shadow and remembered time. Transparent RGBA background, square 1024x1024 sheet, EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows, each cell 256x256, every item separated with generous transparent padding, all centered within own cell. Crisp hand-painted pixel art at logical 2x pixel scale, worn charcoal slate, warm tarnished copper/brass, ember amber accents, bone parchment. No words, no letters, no labels, no background, no gradients outside objects, no mockup screenshot. Row 1 cells left to right: empty dark large square panel with slim carved brass corners and 32px border suitable for nine-slicing; empty rectangular card frame with black inset; horizontal carved dark button plaque; circular glowing lantern medallion. Row 2: lantern icon, flame icon, anatomical stylized heart/crystal health icon, glass oil vial icon. Row 3: folded aged map icon, compass rose icon, open journal icon, doorway/return icon. Row 4: ember cup icon, shadow claw icon, hourglass icon, crossed-out speaker/mute icon. UI must be understated legible dark-fantasy and materially textured, not ornate gold fantasy mobile-game clutter. Empty frames have simple flat dark interiors so text can be rendered separately. Each icon sharp and readable at 32px.
stall: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent game sprite sheet, two variants of THE SAME medieval toy merchant stall in a dark 2.5D side-scrolling pixel-art village. Wide 1536x1024 canvas with a perfect two-column layout; one stall centered in each half with transparent padding and matching pixel coordinates. Left stall closed, right stall open after rescue. Orthographic straight-on side-view platformer, no ground plane or backdrop, no camera tilt. Weathered mossy timber side posts, low stone footings, faded oxblood-and-ochre cloth awning with torn hem, a flat sturdy timber ROOF at the exact same top y in both variants that a character can walk on, subtle toys/cards/wooden bird on a small counter. Closed variant has a horizontally slatted wooden shutter; open variant has shutter rolled up leaving a dark interior opening and visible counter. No people, no text, no signs, no fire, no props outside the stall. Rich restrained hand-painted pixel art matching ruined medieval village with chunky crisp pixels, desaturated night blues, dark brown timber, muted warm red fabric, understated amber highlights. NOT a clean vector drawing or cartoon kiosk. Entire stall and feet within cell; same roof, supports and awning in both variants. Actual transparent background.
